To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the elastic block polymer scaffolds combined with TGF-beta 1 complexed with chitosan and chondroitin-6-sulfate are suitable matrices for cell-based cartilaginous tissue engineering.

the elastic block co-polymer scaffolds with CS-bound TGF-β3 can be a good candidate as a matrix for cell-based chondrogenesis and that the scaffold can be used for chondrogenic differentiation and cartilage tissue regeneration.
rMSCs embedded with a CS-bound, TGF-beta 2-encapsulated scaffold exhibit superior cartilage tissue differentiation as measured by an analysis of gene and protein expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel scaffold system for cartilage tissue engineering using mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs).
the development of a new scaffold for cartilage tissue engineering using a block copolymer scaffold and a CS-bound growth factor.
the development of a tissue engineering scaffold that is capable of promoting cartilage tissue formation in vivo.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the elastic block polymer scaffold with a CS-bound growth factor is a promising material for cell-based cartilaginous tissue engineering.
the elastic block-copolymer scaffolds mixed with CS-bound TGF- beta 3 are very suitable for cell-based cartilaginous tissue engineering.
the CS-bound growth factor complexed scaffolds can provide the most optimal environment for chondrogenic differentiation and cartilage tissue formation of the embedded rMSs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the elastic block polymer scaffold with CS-bound TGF-β3 can provide a good matrix for chondrogenic differentiation and cartilage tissue engineering of rMSCs.
the CS-bound growth factor can be used as a novel delivery system to control the differentiation of transplants cells.
the elastic block polymer scaffolds combined with CS-bound TGF beta 3 are very suitable matrices for cell-based cartilaginous tissue engineering.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a CS-bound TFG-beta 3 is a useful tool for the chondrogenesis for MSCs embedded in a scaffold.
we have developed a method of using a biodegradable scaffold for cartilage tissue engineering by long-term release TGF-beta 2 from chondroitin sulphate.
the scaffold combined with a CS-conjugated TGF-beta 2 is a very suitable matrix for rMSC-based cartilage tissue regeneration.
